definitions.explanation: A small wooden plaque sold at Shinto shrines and Buddhist temples on which worshippers write their prayers or wishes. Originally depicted horses as offerings to the gods.

examples.japanese: {絵馬|えま}に{合格|ごうかく}の{願|ねが}いを{書|か}いた。
examples.english: I wrote my wish to pass the exam on an ema.

examples.japanese: {神社|じんじゃ}には{絵馬|えま}がたくさん{掛|か}けられていた。
examples.english: Many ema were hung at the shrine.

examples.japanese: {絵馬|えま}を{奉納|ほうのう}して{祈願|きがん}する。
examples.english: One makes a wish by dedicating an ema.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
{絵|え} (picture) + {馬|うま} (horse)
Originally, real horses were donated to shrines. Later, pictures of horses were substituted, eventually evolving into wooden tablets.

USAGE:
1. Purchase an {絵馬|えま} at the shrine/temple
2. Write your wish on the back
3. Hang it at the designated place

DESIGNS:
Ema often feature:
- The shrine's deity or symbol
- The current year's zodiac animal
- Anime/manga characters (at some shrines)

COMMON WISHES:
- {合格|ごうかく}: passing exams
- {健康|けんこう}: health
- {縁結|えんむす}び: finding love
- {安産|あんざん}: safe childbirth
